title: Deterministic artifact fingerprinting, reproducible conversion, and pin backstop
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem summary: our current open-weights intake accepts many weight formats and produces runtime artifacts but we lack a deterministic, auditable fingerprint and a reproducible conversion pipeline. That makes it hard to: (1) reproduce a failing smoke test, (2) prove artifact provenance for security/compliance reviews, and (3) implement an automated pin backstop that rolls to a confirmed-good previous pin when a new pin fails performance or safety gates.

Goal: implement an end-to-end flow that produces a canonical artifact bundle with a stable fingerprint (content + conversion recipe + container hash), deterministic conversion with strict seed/control over non-determinism, an automated smoke/canary validation harness that publishes pass/fail telemetry, and a pin backstop orchestration that can revert pin assignments automatically when regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Conversion produces a canonical artifact bundle (.tar.gz) containing converted weights, conversion_manifest.json (schema v1), and container image digest; bundle SHA256 is stable across repeated conversions from the same source and conversion commit.
Conversion pipeline declares and records all non-deterministic knobs (random seeds, parallelism, quantization nondet flags) in conversion_manifest.json so runtime can reproduce same steps.

Automated smoke suite (deterministic prompt set + fixed RNG) executes during onboarding and returns deterministic inference outputs within a tiny epsilon for float targets; results are stored in the model profile.

Pin backstop policy: when a new pin is published and smoke/perf checks fail above configured thresholds, the orchestrator automatically reassigns the previous pin and emits an incident + rollback PR to the catalog.
Telemetry: onboarding emits artifact_fingerprint, conversion_commit, smoke_result (pass/fail), baseline_delta metrics (latency/cost/quality) to the onboarding dashboard for audit/review.
End-to-end docs and runbook checked in: Confluence onboarding spec + runbook for manual rollback and triage steps.
Unit & integration tests for the reproducibility harness are merged and green on main with deterministic CI images pinned by digest.
implementation_steps: Design conversion_manifest schema v1 and finalize required fields (source_uri, source_digest, conversion_commit, toolchain_version, container_digest, rng_control, quantization_profile, deterministic_flags).

Add deterministic conversion wrapper: pin Python/Rust toolchain versions, fix torch/transformers seeds where applicable, serialize parallelism/layout knobs in manifest, and produce canonical file ordering during tar creation.

Build deterministic smoke harness: canonical prompt set repo, fixed tokenizer versions, single-threaded inference run in CI image pinned by digest, diff outputs with epsilon thresholds and store results in onboarding DB.
Implement fingerprinting service change: compute SHA256 over canonical bundle bytes and record as artifact_fingerprint; index in catalog and surface in Console model page.

Create pin backstop controller: on publish-pin event, subscribe to smoke_result stream; if smoke_result.fail OR baseline_delta.quality < -X% then trigger backstop workflow to reassign previous pin and open incident ticket + PR to catalog.
Add telemetry events and dashboard panels for audit: ingestion timeline, fingerprint map, smoke pass rate, rollback events, and distribution of baseline_delta metrics.
Write runbook and Confluence doc with triage flow, expected logs, and steps for manual intervention.
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Draft spec completed and shared with PM & Security for initial feedback. Added initial conversion_manifest fields. (Marisol)

2025-02-22: Spike completed: ran three repeated conversions of llama-3-small weights -> canonical bundle matched SHA256 across runs using pinned builder image. Recorded notes about nondet quantize stage. (Ibrahim)

2025-02-25: Security review raised question about including source credentials in manifest. Decided to record source_uri and source_digest but keep any secrets out of manifest; add signed provenance metadata instead. (Security: Priya R.)

2025-02-28: Prototype smoke harness integrated into CI with deterministic prompt set. Observed minor tokenization diffs between tokenizers v0.11 and v0.12; pinned tokenizer version in harness. (Ibrahim)

2025-03-03: Began implementation of pin backstop controller; created event contract for publish-pin -> onboarding.done which includes artifact_fingerprint and smoke_result. Implemented simple test harness for auto-reassign. (Ibrahim)
2025-03-04: PR #7121 opened to add conversion_manifest schema & bundle creation code. Requesting review from @emily and @jonah for telemetry fields. (Ibrahim)
comments: Jonah (PM): Please ensure the smoke prompt set includes edge safety cases we saw in the incident last month. Also include metric thresholds in the spec so ops can tune. (2025-02-19)
Priya (Security): Good to include signed provenance; recommend using our KMS signing flow to sign the manifest and publish signature alongside the bundle. Avoid secrets in manifests. (2025-02-25)
Emily (Observability): We need a unique event namespace for onboarding.telemetry.artifact_fingerprint to avoid collisions with runtime events. Also add token-level cost delta as a field. (2025-03-02)
Ibrahim (Eng): Note: quantization step in OSS converter uses nondet multithreading in C++; adding --deterministic-quant flag and single-thread fallback. Will add details in PR. (2025-02-22)
Marisol (Creator): After merge, schedule a canary onboarding run on a low-traffic dedicated pool to validate backstop behavior end-to-end before enabling auto-reassign for all customers. (2025-03-04)
